newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps up, CFDs gains 10 ct, fuel climbs.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps up, CFDs gains 10 ct, fuel climbs.

text.p: European oil swaps firmed on Friday morning after mostly slipping lower on Thursday.
Dealers said demand in Asia remained strong and was helping to counter the persistent weakness of crude oil markets in the West.
"It just feels very neutral still. The Med has got support from Singapore but otherwise the market is still weak," said a fuel trader.
Gasoline nudged up 50 cents a tonne to $193 for May and $190.50 for June. No early trade was reported.
Gasoline crack spreads against Brent were little changed with June at $4.95 a barrel and the third and fourth quarters were pegged around $4.10 and $3.10 respectively.
Gas oil against Brent remained well bid but levels were little changed from Tuesday at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Jet premiums were flat after edging higher on Thursday. May held around $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that levels on Thursday. The third and fourth quarters holding at $27.25 and $32 above the screen respectively.
Heavy fuel edged up to $1 a tonne to $82.75 for May barges and $87 for low sulphur. The Mediterranean held around $75.50 to $76 for May amid support from Singapore which held at $98.00.
Dealers said the market remained depressed in Europe with only minimal demand from power companies and shipowners.
Brent CFDs firmed with next week trading at just 50 cents under June compared to around 60 cents under on Thursday and the following week talked 47 cents under, or some 8 cents higher.
The following two weeks were unchanged at 43 cents and 37 cents under respectively.
